hero.lede: I study what people notice, miss, trust, and disclose when they use generative AI. I also build the study tools behind that work: chat interfaces, annotation workflows, and privacy dashboards.
hero.context: PhD candidate in Computer Science at The George Washington University.

howIWork.label: Study
howIWork.value: I run studies of how people interpret AI responses, decide what to trust, and recognize privacy or safety problems.

howIWork.label: Build
howIWork.value: I write the software those studies run on — from survey flow to chat backend to the pipeline that exports clean data for analysis.

howIWork.label: Apply
howIWork.value: I use the results to show where current evaluation methods fall short — and what evidence product teams and regulators would need instead.

jobSearch.text: I'm looking for research and research-engineering roles. If your team evaluates AI systems with real users — or needs the tooling to do it — I'd like to talk.

projectsPage.lede: Four projects: an open-source study platform, the published auditing study that ran on it, and two studies still in the field.

publicationsPage.lede: Peer-reviewed and preprint work on how people judge AI chatbots, how studies should measure those judgments, and how privacy information reaches — or fails to reach — users.

cvPage.lede: Education, publications, research experience, and the systems behind them, in one PDF.
cvPage.summary: PhD candidate in Computer Science (usable security and privacy; trustworthy AI) at The George Washington University, advised by Adam Aviv. Recent work spans chatbot auditing studies, privacy-label measurement, and the software that runs them.

researchProfile.label: Research
researchProfile.value: Human-centered evaluation, AI auditing, trust, privacy, and governance of generative AI.

researchProfile.label: Methods
researchProfile.value: Interactive experiments, large-scale online studies, interviews, surveys, qualitative analysis, and mixed methods.

researchProfile.label: Systems
researchProfile.value: Evaluation interfaces, auditing workflows, AI interaction-history dashboards, study platforms, and human-data infrastructure.

researchProfile.label: Currently
researchProfile.value: PhD candidate in Computer Science at The George Washington University, advised by Adam Aviv.
